messages:
maya: noticing a perf regression on the new SM92 nodes when serving long sequences (>2k). landing traces show we fall back to the generic attention kernel.
kevin: ugh, any detect output from the startup probe? might be mis-detecting FP8 or tensor core support.
maya: pasted the probe run from one affected node:
```
$ ./cuda-cap-detect --summary
GPU 0: NVIDIA A10X-SMX (SM 9.2)
Supports: CUDA 12.2, TensorCores: yes, BF16: yes
FP8 runtime support: unknown
cuBLASLt kernels: ok
fused_mha: not available (driver fallback)
KV-cache optimized paths: enabled
autobatching: enabled
```
kevin: "FP8 runtime support: unknown" stands out. our kernel router requires explicit FP8 flag for the new fused-fmha path. if probe returns unknown, we choose the generic kernel.
anya: did the probe binary get the new NV driver ABI? we added FP8 checks in v0.12 probe.
diego: checking the boot logs — some nodes still have CUDA 12.0 packages, even though the driver is 535.x. partial ABI mismatch could make FP8 feature probes skip.
kevin: can you share the perf numbers? how big is the regression?
maya: microbench on 16B LLaMA variant, batch=4, seqlen=2048 -> 4096
- before (fused_mha): 12.4 ms/token
- after (fallback generic): 18.7 ms/token
~50% slower for HF-like decode loads :disappointed:
ci-bot: nightly perf job 2026-03-14 posted: https://perf.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/2026-03-14 (summary attached)
ops-bot: pinned nodes with driver mismatch for quarantine: node-rt-13, node-rt-14 :warning:
kevin: short term: add an override flag in runtime to force FP8/TensorCore-enabled kernel selection for queued requests on those nodes (opt-in).
anya: long term: probe needs to validate FP8 by trying a tiny fp8 SGEMM candidate kernel at startup rather than relying on driver feature enums.
diego: also saw increased KV-cache hits changing behavior after fallback — the generic kernel spends more time in KV encode, so cache prefetch windows need to expand. that might be compounding latency.
maya: good catch. I instrumented KV timings — encode phase went from 1.3ms to 3.9ms on fallback. decode token spend is now heavily skewed.
kevin: plan: (1) release a hotfix probe v0.12.1 that validates FP8 via microkernel; (2) add runtime flag RECOMMEND_FP8=true for canary nodes; (3) temporarily route long seq jobs to older SM nodes with known FP8 support; (4) tune KV-prefetch window when fused_mha not used.
anya: I'll open PRs for probe and runtime flag. will include a small non-invasive microkernel test snippet:
```
// FP8 microprobe pseudocode
allocate small tensors on GPU
launch fp8_test_gemm(A_fp8, B_fp8, C_fp8)
check for correct completion and non-NaN output
```
maya: created an incident ticket and linked the perf dashboard. tagging ops to roll quarantine nodes back to staging.
ops-bot: quarantine rollback scheduled in 20m for node-rt-13 if probe passes.
kevin: also add a metric for "kernel-fallback-rate" per host so we can alert when >1% of requests hit generic path for seqlen>1024.
diego: I'll push a KV-prefetch PR after we stabilize probe. should reduce the encode penalty by ~40% when fused_mha is missing.
maya: thanks all — this explains the spike in p95s. I'll monitor and follow up with regression numbers after hotfix.
kevin: :thumbsup: keep staged canary until next rollback window.
ci-bot: perf CI run (canary) finished: delta p95 latency +24% on canary nodes (details: https://perf.internal/redwood/compare/canary-185123)
anya: noted, will include those deltas in the PR description.
maya: filing follow-up to track automatic kernel preference adjustments based on observed seqlen histogram per-route.
kevin: good. once probe and metric are in, we can automate fallback thresholds instead of manual flags.
